-# kvstore: a replicated key-value store on vsr-rs
+# kvstore
 
-A small key-value store replicated with Viewstamped Replication. Each node
-runs one `vsr_rs::Replica`. Nodes talk to each other over TCP, and every
-node accepts client connections speaking a Redis-like inline protocol, so a
-plain `nc` session works as a client. Reads and writes both go through the
-replicated log, so a `GET` returns the value of the latest committed `SET`
-no matter which node answers it.
+A key-value store replicated with vsr-rs. Every node accepts clients over a
+Redis-like inline protocol, so `nc` works.
 
-It uses the standard library for networking and threads, and nothing else.
+## Run
 
-## Starting a cluster
-
-Build the example once:
+Build and start three nodes, each in its own terminal:
 
 ```console
 cargo build --example kvstore
-```
-
-Then start three nodes, each in its own terminal. Every node gets the same
-list of replica addresses, its own index into that list, and an address to
-accept clients on:
-
-```console
 ./target/debug/examples/kvstore --id 0 --replicas 127.0.0.1:7000,127.0.0.1:7001,127.0.0.1:7002 --listen 127.0.0.1:6379
 ./target/debug/examples/kvstore --id 1 --replicas 127.0.0.1:7000,127.0.0.1:7001,127.0.0.1:7002 --listen 127.0.0.1:6380
 ./target/debug/examples/kvstore --id 2 --replicas 127.0.0.1:7000,127.0.0.1:7001,127.0.0.1:7002 --listen 127.0.0.1:6381
 ```
 
-Each node prints who the primary is, and again whenever that changes:
-
-```console
-node 0 of 3: replicas on 127.0.0.1:7000, clients on 127.0.0.1:6379, primary is node 0
-```
-
-Set `RUST_LOG=info` to see nodes connecting to each other, or `RUST_LOG=trace`
-to see every protocol message.
-
-## Talking to it
-
-Connect to any node with `nc`. Commands are one per line; keys and values
-are single words.
+Talk to any node:
 
 ```console
 $ nc localhost 6379
@@ -54,58 +29,12 @@ GET nope
 $-1
 ```
 
-A node that is not the primary forwards the request to the primary and
-routes the reply back, so this works just the same against port 6380 or
-6381.
-
-## Killing the primary
-
-With the three nodes running, stop node 0 with Ctrl-C. Within about half a
-second the other two notice the silence, run a view change, and node 1
-becomes the primary of view 1:
-
-```console
-view 1: primary is node 1 (this node)
-```
-
-Clients connected to node 1 or node 2 keep working. A request that was in
-flight when the primary died is re-sent by the node holding the client
-connection until it gets a reply, and the new primary answers it once,
-even if it arrives more than once.
-
-Start node 0 again with the same command line and it rejoins the cluster
-as a backup of view 1, fetching the log it missed from the new primary.
-
-## How it works
-
-- Each node has one thread that owns the replica and everything that must
-  stay single-threaded. Every other thread turns the outside world into
-  events for it: lines from peer connections, commands from client
-  connections, and a tick every 100 milliseconds that drives the
-  replica's heartbeats, retransmissions, and view change timer.
-- Protocol messages travel between nodes as one line of text each. See
-  `encode` and `decode` in `main.rs`. Connections to peers are opened on
-  demand and dropped on error; the protocol re-sends anything that
-  matters.
-- Every client connection gets its own `vsr_rs::Client`, with a client id
-  that encodes the node it is connected to. The primary sends the reply to
-  that node, which writes it to the connection. Ids also include the
-  node's start time, so a restarted node never reuses an id: the primary
-  would otherwise take a new connection's first request for a re-send of
-  an old one and answer it from its client table.
-- A `SET` becomes a `Put` op and a `GET` becomes a `Get` op in the log.
-  The state machine is a `HashMap` behind a mutex; the output of an op is
-  the value a `Get` read.
+Stop node 0 with Ctrl-C. The others pick node 1 as the new primary within
+a second and keep serving. Start node 0 again and it rejoins as a backup.
 
-## Limitations
+## Notes
 
-- Nothing is written to disk. A node that restarts comes back empty and
-  catches up from the primary, which is fine for a demo but not what the
-  paper's recovery protocol does: a replica that forgot what it
-  acknowledged can, in rare interleavings, let a view change lose a
-  committed op. vsr-rs does not implement recovery yet.
-- Keys and values are single words: the inline protocol splits on
-  whitespace, and so does the encoding between nodes.
-- One command at a time per connection, matching the one outstanding
-  request per client in the paper.
-- No authentication, no persistence, no reconfiguration. It is an example.
+- Keys and values are single words. One command at a time per connection.
+- Nothing is stored on disk. A restarted node comes back empty and catches
+  up from the primary.
+- `RUST_LOG=trace` shows every protocol message.
